item.title: Physics-informed neural networks for viscoelastic fluid flows around a cylinder in a two-dimensional channel
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Midhuna Suresh, Akanksha Gupta
arXiv:2609.07861v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Grid-based fluid dynamics solvers routinely struggle with exhaustive meshing demands and ill-posed inverse problems. A practical mesh-free alternative is given by Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) but, applying them to highly elastic Oldroyd-B fluids results in many training failures. The High Weissenberg Number Problem (HWNP), driven by the exponential stress growth near stagnation points is a major issue, which causes standard PINN optimizers to diverge. To prevent the network from crashing, we apply a Cholesky decomposition to the conformation tensor. This mathematical constraint stabilizes the gradients by guaranteeing a positive-definite stress field. Beyond mathematical stability, the inherent spectral bias of deep learning mode…

item.title: Solving the Elastic Wave Equation with Physics-Informed Neural Networks: A Robust and Critical Assessment
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Davide Staub, Ben Moseley
arXiv:2609.07983v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) have recently emerged as a promising approach for solving Partial Differential Equations (PDEs), offering a meshfree alternative that integrates physical principles into the learning process. This presents a new paradigm compared to traditional discretization methods and purely data-driven machine learning techniques. While promising, PINNs are not a panacea; they inherit challenges such as spectral bias and unstable convergence. Moreover, their potential in seismology remains largely unexplored. In this work, we provide a robust and critical assessment of PINNs for solving the elastic wave equation in seismology. We investigate the performance of PINNs on problems with varying degrees of complexity a…

item.title: Topology Obstructs Pure Foundation Neural Quantum States
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Timothy Heightman, Elena Orlova, Philip Mantrov, Aleksei Ustimenko
arXiv:2609.07591v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Foundation models for ground states in spin-1/2 systems are a promising method for problems ranging from quantum chemistry to identifying new phase diagrams. Nearly all such models are currently pure-states that condition on the Hamiltonian's parameters, whose Monte Carlo samples give energy estimates according to the variational principle. In this contribution, we show that this representation is topologically obstructed. For any gapped Hamiltonian family whose ground-state bundle is non-trivial, every continuous normalized state-vector model has zero fidelity with the ground state at some parameter value in the Hamiltonian family. For that value, the energy is at least one spectral gap, Δ, with an O(Δ) gap in an open-neighbourhood of tha…

item.title: Metal-Insulator Transition Classification Using Hybrid Quantum Learning Under Data Scarcity
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Gourab Datta, Sara Aminpour, Sarah Sharif, Yaser Banad
Metal–insulator transition (MIT) materials are promising for electronic, sensing, and neuromorphic technologies, but their data-driven classification remains challenging because experimentally verified examples are scarce, heterogeneous, and strongly imbalanced. We evaluate whether compact quantum classifiers provide useful predictive readouts under these conditions without assuming or claiming quantum advantage. In a protocol-controlled hybrid graph–quantum benchmark, fold-local crystal graph convolutional neural networks are trained on 316 structure-available compounds, and their frozen embeddings are supplied to linear, multilayer-perceptron, variational quantum circuit (VQC), and data re-uploading (REUP) heads. This work demonstrates that Fourier Neural Operators (FNOs), combined with wavelet-based encodings of PDE inputs, can learn and predict multiple eigenmodes of the elastic wave equation, corresponding to deformation modes of acoustic waves propagating through arbitrary metamaterial geometries. PPIM builds on the temporal subse…

item.title: 稀土倍半氧化物表面无势垒水解离的第一性原理研究
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Shuxiang Zhou, Jay A. LaVerne, Hanna Hlushko

item.title: 用于粉末X射线衍射多相识别的可扩展机器学习框架
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Xinyang Tong, Ethan Jin, Jiahan Xu, Aditya Rao, Pengcen Jiang, Nathan J. Szymanski
该研究提出GALAXI，将粉末X射线衍射相识别拆分为多个独立的一对其余二分类器，再结合Rietveld精修确定最佳相组合。该方法在实验图谱数据集上达到0.935的micro-F1分数，优于传统检索匹配和既有深度学习模型，并能抵抗低杂质相含量、晶粒尺寸小、峰位偏移、样品位移和织构等常见实验伪影。由于相专属模型相互独立，GALAXI可扩展到大型参考库而无需重训既有模型。

item.title: 低雷诺数下后缘变形翼型快速气动预测的物理信息机器学习框架
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Siddalingappa P Kodigaddi
本文提出并验证了一个物理信息机器学习代理框架，用于快速预测低雷诺数后缘变形翼型的气动性能。该框架基于456个ANSYS Fluent算例，比较了随机森林、梯度提升、多层感知器和高斯过程回归四种模型，并同时预测升力、阻力、俯仰力矩、升阻比及表面压力指标。结果表明，物理信息特征工程可使预测误差最多降低18%，梯度提升模型具有较高精度，高斯过程回归则能识别后失速高不确定性区域；设计空间分析显示，抛物线襟翼在所研究条件下普遍优于传统襟翼。

However, most existing global neural operators for PDEs require large training datasets and many learnable parameters, with limited interpretability and generalization. 👤 Erin R. Johnson, Kyle R. Bryenton
arXiv:2609.06162v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Delocalisation error has been argued to be the greatest outstanding challenge in density-functional theory (DFT). item.title: 合成反铁磁畴壁上的交错阻尼型自旋轨道力矩理论
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Yuta Yamane, Takeshi Seki
该研究提出了合成反铁磁体中交错阻尼型自旋轨道力矩的理论，指出其可在两侧夹有相同重金属的合成反铁磁体中普遍产生。通过推导Néel矢量拉格朗日量，作者得到畴壁速度的闭式表达：其与电流和面内场呈双线性关系，对Néel壁和Bloch壁符号相反，并可通过层间交换耦合调控。微磁模拟验证了理论，并给出可直接实验检验的符号反转、标度律和Néel-Bloch转变阈值。

item.title: Open-source implementation of the anti-Hermitian contracted Schrödinger equation for electronic ground and excited states
item.description:
📚 The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue
Efficient simulation of strongly correlated electrons has become a routine tool in molecular electronic structure theory due to recent advances in approximate configuration interaction (CI) techniques. Nonetheless, the quantitative and predictive description of molecular electronic states remains a significant challenge due to the difficulty of computing all-electron correlation beyond CI. Here, we describe a new open-source implementation of the anti-Hermitian contracted Schrödinger equation (ACSE) for use in accurate simulation of all-electron correlation in molecules. In contrast to standard approaches via multireference perturbation theory, the scaling of the ACSE does not depend on the complexity of the strongly correlated reference wavefunction. item.title: Phase-resolved imaging of coherent phonon-magnon coupling
item.description:
📚 Editors' Suggestions
👤 Yannik Kunz, Florian Kraft, David Breitbach, Kevin Künstle, Torben Pfeifer, Matthias Küß 等9位作者
Author(s): Yannik Kunz, Florian Kraft, David Breitbach, Kevin Künstle, Torben Pfeifer, Matthias Küß, Stephan Glamsch, Manfred Albrecht, and Mathias Weiler The interaction between surface acoustic waves and spin waves may open new routes for compact and efficient passive microwave devices. The design of such devices requires understanding of the magnetoacoustic phenomena. Here, the authors use phase-resolved micro-optical imaging to detect and discriminate both types of waves in their micropatterned device. By tuning the magnetic field, the authors directly image the resonant magnetoacoustic coupling and provide experimental evidence for the coherent excitation of spin waves by the traveling acoustic wave. [Phys. Rev. B 114, L140403] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026
